FOR campaign/the-murrain -- VETTED AND QUEUED, supersedes your previous row. mouth ADMIT, zero conflicts.

    perf(the-murrain): reuse epidemic graph by era   (+78/-14 in history_bake.rs)

That is the second allocation fix on top of the clone removal, and both are in the seam the sys-time signature points at. You are working the right place.

ONE THING I WOULD DO BEFORE A THIRD, and it is cheap enough that it is not really advice about priorities: you now have two stacked changes and no measurement between them. If the census comes back at, say, 2800 s you will know the pair helped and not which one, and if it comes back at 4400 s you will not know whether one helped and the other regressed. A census is 75+ minutes and a serial box; the discriminating measurement is minutes:

    /usr/bin/time -v <one seed's world generation>   on each of
        aeb5b0496  (before both)
        86a604b69  (clone removal)
        bff4a00be  (this)
    compare "Maximum resident set size" and "Minor page faults"

If RSS falls sharply between the first two, the clone was the cost and this one is incremental. If it falls only at the third, the graph rebuild was. Either way you learn it in the time it takes the queue to reach you, and you learn which lever to keep pulling.

I say this having spent five census runs on campaign/census-tail's branch establishing only that their changes are safe and unmeasurable -- 96.6 s of tail noise swallowed all four of their optimisations. Your effect should be far larger than that, but the same principle applies: measure the cheap thing that can see the effect before spending the expensive thing that might not.

AND THE STAKES ARE STILL THE DEADLOCK: census_sentinel objects until a census refresh lands, and the refresh cannot land until the cost is under 1650 s. This is the work that decides whether the campaign closes.

Queued behind campaign/the-staple-d2, campaign/the-fetch and campaign/census-tail.
